name: @yourtal/ledger-service
//: This file exists so turbo SEES the Go services. `services/*` was already in
pnpm-workspace.yaml, but without a package.json pnpm and turbo skipped it
entirely — so `pnpm verify`, the named repo gate, ran 282 TypeScript test
files and ZERO Go ones. The ledger, the invariant checker, the daily Merkle
proof and every voucher tamper test sat outside the only gate anyone runs.
-count=1 is REQUIRED, not tidiness. Go caches test results per package, and
on 2026-09-20 a cached `ok` hid a genuinely failing invariant check. A gate
that may answer from cache is not a gate.
-p 1 is REQUIRED for correctness, not speed. Go runs package test binaries
concurrently, and these packages share ONE Postgres. internal/proof
deliberately unbalances ledger.entry to prove tampering is detected, while
internal/ledger asserts the whole ledger is balanced. Run in parallel they
race. See YT-0567 for the real fix; this flag makes the gate deterministic
